title: Welcome to Software Development
learning_outcomes: Describe a software lifecycle and turn needs into testable requirements.
Decompose work into slices and design focused modules with clear interfaces.
Use version-control, review, testing, debugging, and documentation practices.
Build security, accessibility, privacy, and maintainability into development work.
Plan, release, and maintain a small software product honestly and safely.

sections.heading: What is Software Development?
sections.body: Software development is the organised work of understanding a problem, planning a solution, building it, checking it, releasing it, and maintaining it. Think of it like planning and constructing a school building: people agree on what is needed, make a plan, build carefully, inspect the result, and look after it.

sections.heading: Why is it useful?
sections.body: Software development helps create systems for school records, small-business stock, farm planning, public information, and everyday digital services. A disciplined process helps teams build tools that people can understand, trust, use safely, and improve over time.

sections.heading: What can you build or do with it?
sections.body: You will learn to describe a need as clear requirements, divide work into manageable parts, design modules, and use version control, review, testing, debugging, and documentation. You will also consider security, accessibility, privacy, release, and maintenance while building a small software product.

sections.heading: How to use these lessons
sections.body: Read the situation and explanation first, predict what a good solution should do, and then try the planning or coding activity. Use the knowledge checks to confirm key ideas and the activities to practise decisions; explain why you chose an approach instead of only recording that it worked.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: You do not need professional software-development experience, but you should be able to read simple Python code and use a school-approved development environment. A computer is recommended; internet helps with collaboration and resources, while some planning, coding, and testing activities can be completed offline.
